analysis.investment_thesis: Excelsoft is a reasonably priced EdTech SaaS micro-cap riding India's education digitisation wave, with 17.7% revenue CAGR and near-zero debt — but volatile profitability, a sub-par ROE of 10.4%, and suspicious quality of FY25 earnings keep conviction low. At EV/EBITDA of 6x and forward P/E of 13x, the valuation is not demanding, but better entry discipline is warranted.
key_strengths: Rapid debt deleveraging: borrowings collapsed from INR 168 Cr (2020) to INR 45 Cr (2025), D/E now a clean 0.12
Steady revenue growth at 17.7% 5Y CAGR (103→233 Cr) with 5/5 years of positive OCF (~53–63 Cr range)
Cheap on forward multiples — Forward P/E 13x and EV/EBITDA 5.98x for a global SaaS business in the high-growth EdTech segment
key_risks: Profitability is volatile and low-quality: net profit swung 22→13→35 Cr in three years; FY25 surge partly inflated by other income jumping to INR 15 Cr from INR 2 Cr in FY24
ROE of 10.4% is well below my 20%+ threshold — capital is not being deployed efficiently despite the asset-light SaaS model
EBITDA trend is contracting (8.1% 5Y CAGR, labelled contracting) even as revenue grows — margin dilution is a structural concern
red_flags: FY25 'Other Income' surged 650% YoY (INR 2→15 Cr) — this propped up net profit to 35 Cr; strip it out and underlying earnings growth looks far weaker
FCF reported as INR 290 Cr in FY25 while OCF was only 53 Cr — likely a data anomaly or one-off asset monetisation that is not repeatable
Micro-cap (INR 812 Cr) with very low FII interest (1.37%) and limited institutional coverage — liquidity and discovery risk are real
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Excelsoft is a 25-year-old Mysore-based EdTech SaaS player offering assessment, proctoring, and LMS products to universities, schools and enterprises globally — a genuinely interesting niche riding India's digital education push and the global online examination boom post-COVID. Revenue has grown consistently at 17.7% CAGR from INR 103 Cr to 233 Cr, capex is minimal (~17 Cr/year), and the promoter has aggressively paid down debt, cutting borrowings by ~73% over five years to just INR 45 Cr. At EV/EBITDA of 6x and a forward P/E of 13x, the street is not pricing in much optimism, which creates a floor on downside. The 59% promoter holding is stable and comfortable.

However, the quality of the business is not what I need for a high-conviction bet. ROE at 10.4% is mediocre — a true SaaS compounder should be generating 25–35% ROE, not 10%. EBITDA has actually contracted in trend terms despite top-line growth, signalling either pricing pressure or rising costs. Most worryingly, the FY25 net profit of INR 35 Cr rests partly on INR 15 Cr of "other income" — up from just INR 2 Cr the year before — whose nature is opaque. I will not pay even a modest multiple for earnings built on non-recurring items. For existing shareholders, hold while the deleveraging story plays out and wait for clarity on sustainable operating margins; fresh capital should demand a cleaner earnings print before entering.
